doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Vocalese and Lambert, Hendricks and Ross
title: Love as the strongest force, King and the Black Panthers
summary: Hendricks argues love disarms racism, citing Gandhi, King and the Sermon on the Mount.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Sure. So we went. We had the time of our lives, and they had the time of their lives. They loved us. That was the result of it. So it shows, once again, that people create these monsters that they make you afraid of, and that in truth, nothing exists of any power stronger than love. Love is the strongest force in the universe. Mahatma Ghandi used Jesus Christ’s Sermon on the Mount and drove the British out of India. They’ve been trying for a thousand years to do that. Martin Luther King in turn used the Sermon on the Mount and changed the face of the South forever. You can’t fight love. See hate, they can fight that. They can lynch you, and they can kill you. But if you love them, they can’t fight you. You disarm them. It’s a very strong force, and it’s what Christ preached. Christ in the New Testament brought man from the Mosaic law into the law of the psychology, the psychological law. If a man hits you, and you say, “I love you,” you drive him nuts. He gets so mad he hits you again, and you say, “Why are you hitting me when I love you?” Then he just drops his weapon and starts to weep, because you call upon the essential humanity that is in him. He is, after all, a man and a human being, and you call upon this humanity. You call if forth past the beast that’s manifesting and beating you. You call him into being the essential him. That’s why . . .

That’s why they shot Reverend King, because he did that. They love it if you hate them. Then they can kill you. Look at the Black Panthers. They were going to fight back. In two months, 30 of them were dead. Love is the strongest force in the universe.
I tell you. That is very evident for me in your lyrics. There are just so many different songs where love is the key word and the key feeling, the philosophy in those lyrics.
